blocks.prompt: 7. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\).
blocks.explanation:
The right side contains \(x\) only (\(h(y) = 1\)), so the equation is separable: \(y = \int f(x)\,dx\).
Plan: break the fraction into partial fractions, integrate each part, and combine the logarithms.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\).
To find: the general solution.
Method: separable with \(h(y) = 1\), so \(dy = f(x)\,dx\). The fraction has a linear factor and an irreducible quadratic factor, so use partial fractions.

Separate
\[dy = \dfrac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\,dx\]
Why: multiply both sides by \(dx\).

Set up partial fractions
\[\dfrac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)} = \dfrac{A}{1 - x} + \dfrac{Bx + D}{1 + x^2}\]
\[1 + x = A(1 + x^2) + (Bx + D)(1 - x)\]
Why: a linear factor gets a constant on top; the quadratic \(1 + x^2\) (no real roots) gets a linear top.

Find \(A\), \(B\), \(D\)
Put \(x = 1\): \(2 = 2A\), so \(A = 1\).
Coefficients of \(x^2\): \(0 = A - B\), so \(B = 1\).
Constant terms: \(1 = A + D\), so \(D = 0\).
Why: \(x = 1\) makes the second term vanish; the rest come from comparing coefficients. (Coefficient of \(x\): \(1 = B - D\), true.)

Rewrite and integrate
\[dy = \left(\dfrac{1}{1 - x} + \dfrac{x}{1 + x^2}\right)dx\]
\[y = -\ln|1 - x| + \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1 + x^2) + \ln|C|\]
Why: \(\int\frac{dx}{1 - x} = -\ln|1 - x|\) (derivative of \(1 - x\) is \(-1\)); \(\int\frac{x\,dx}{1 + x^2} = \frac{1}{2}\ln(1 + x^2)\) (top is half the derivative of the bottom). The constant is written as \(\ln|C|\).

Combine the logarithms
\[y = \ln\left|\dfrac{C\sqrt{1 + x^2}}{1 - x}\right|\]
Why: \(\frac{1}{2}\ln a = \ln\sqrt{a}\), \(\ln a + \ln b = \ln ab\), \(\ln a - \ln b = \ln\frac{a}{b}\).

Check
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{1 + x^2} + \dfrac{1}{1 - x}\]
\[= \dfrac{x(1 - x) + 1 + x^2}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\]
This is the given right side.
